name: BNO pool stale NFT reward accounting
summary: The pool's emergency withdrawal cleared ERC-20 stake and reward-debt accounting but left the NFT reward addition active, so a later NFT withdrawal could pay rewards that were no longer backed by stake.
notes: Direct contract deployment. Its 13,327-byte runtime hashes to 0x541c5518ef3d2925449174422b64c0b7f93b043f76a507606b6dc845292666be both at deployment block 28522657 and immediately before the campaign; the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, and the runtime contains neither DELEGATECALL nor SELFDESTRUCT.

Exact pre-recovery victim depletion is the BNO balance change of pool 0xdca503449899d5649d32175a255a8835a03e4006 across the two successful campaign transactions: 1,563,370.168598147731548146 BNO immediately before the anchor and zero after the second transaction. The second receipt records 504,557.855800853399893084 USDT paid to campaign funds-holder 0xdc109426972ae14d5b3d7e91b47d42ff1fd3c8cc after the depleted BNO was sold; that exact stablecoin realization at par is used instead of the seed row's rounded USD 505,000 headline or a thin-market spot mark. The attacker's flash liquidity and amounts returned to the pool are not counted separately. No recovery is netted.
The USD value conservatively uses exact campaign-realized USDT proceeds at par rather than an external pre-exploit BNO mark.
